title: Allow server initiated renegotiate when using OpenSSL / BoringSSL bas…

timeline.body:
…ed SSLEngine

Motivation:

We should allow server initiated renegotiation when OpenSSL / BoringSSL bases SSLEngine is used as it might be used for client auth.

Modifications:

- Upgrade netty-tcnative version to be able to allow renegotiate once
- Adjust code

Result
Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11529

Do we just want to always set this to `_ONCE` or would it be better to make this configurable?
SwiftNIO made it configurable, and I don't see a rationale for why we wouldn't do the same.

reply.body: Is this perhaps related to the `SSL.getHandshakeCount(ssl) > 1` check in `rejectRemoteInitiatedRenegotiation()`?

I just thought `_ONCE` should be good enough for the client auth while still add some sort of protection. OpenSSL always just allows it and the JDK as well. SwiftNIO only supports BoringSSL so its a bit easier for them .

timeline.body: Had some questions. Also, I hope you're able to add a test for this.
It looks like this would allow unlimited renegotiation for non-boringssl on client-side. Am I reading this right?

reply.body: Yeah, shutdown and throw is skipped when client-side. This looks suspicious.
yes ... I guess we could still add some guards. Let me do this
